ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ with pseudohorn cysts

s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end of the tumor
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation noted by the patient's wife
Tumor located on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Microscopic findings include hyperkeratotic lesion and pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures present
Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid-Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
Negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains
Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ with pseudohorn cysts

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Microscopic findings include proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, consistent with squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion and pseudohorn cysts are characteristic of keratoacanthoma, and the recent growth and crust formation are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a well-circumscribed papule with a flakier surface and the microscopic findings of a hyperkeratotic lesion are consistent with verrucous carcinoma

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, basal cell carcinoma is still a possible diagnosis given the location and appearance of the tumor, and the presence of mitotic figures

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ with pseudohorn cysts
shortlist.why_kept: The microscopic findings of pseudohorn cysts and the presence of neoplastic squamous cells are consistent with this diagnosis, and it is a plausible rare/can't-miss diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures, supports the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor's recent growth and crust formation, as well as its invasive nature with proliferation into the dermis, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma typically has a more rapid growth phase and often resolves on its own, which does not match the 4-year history of the eyelid mass.

rejected.label: Verrucous carcinoma
rejected.why: Verrucous carcinoma is a low-grade malignancy that typically has a cauliflower-like appearance and is less aggressive, which does not fit the described tumor's recent growth and invasive characteristics.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common skin cancer but typically has different histological features, such as palisading nuclei and clefting around tumor islands, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ with pseudohorn cysts
rejected.why: The presence of invasive malignant squamous cells into the dermis indicates a more aggressive tumor than squamous cell carcinoma in situ, which is confined to the epidermis.
